rubric.why: The cell cycle describes the events between successive cell divisions.
rubric.description: Defines the cell cycle as the series of events from one cell division to the next.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the series of events between successive cell divisions, or an equivalent definition.

rubric.why: Interphase occurs between cell divisions and includes cell growth and DNA replication.
rubric.description: Defines interphase and identifies its main activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining interphase as the period between divisions, or for identifying growth and DNA replication.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the series of events from one cell division to the next.
Interphase is the period between two successive cell divisions, during which the cell grows and replicates its DNA.

items.followUp: State two functions of magnesium in plants.

rubric.why: Potassium activates enzymes in plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzyme activation as a role of potassium.

rubric.why: Potassium helps regulate stomatal movement and is needed for protein synthesis.
rubric.description: Gives another valid role of potassium in plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one further correct role, such as regulating stomatal opening and closing or supporting protein synthesis.

modelAnswer: Potassium activates enzymes in plant cells.
It helps regulate the opening and closing of stomata and is needed for processes such as protein synthesis.

items.followUp: State the functions of red blood cells and plasma.

rubric.why: White blood cells protect the body against disease-causing organisms.
rubric.description: States the defensive function of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that white blood cells defend the body or fight infection or disease.

rubric.why: Platelets help form blood clots and prevent excessive blood loss.
rubric.description: States the role of platelets in blood clotting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying clot formation or prevention of blood loss.

modelAnswer: White blood cells defend the body against infection and disease.
Platelets help in blood clotting and prevent excessive blood loss.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and functions of mitochondria.

rubric.why: The nucleus is enclosed by a double-membraned nuclear envelope.
rubric.description: Describes the nuclear envelope as a double membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the double nuclear membrane.

rubric.description: Identifies pores in the nuclear envelope.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nuclear envelope has pores.

rubric.why: The nucleus contains nucleoplasm and chromatin, which is made of DNA and proteins and forms chromosomes during cell division.
rubric.description: Names a correct component inside the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying nucleoplasm or chromatin/chromosomes containing DNA.

rubric.why: The nucleus controls and coordinates the activities of the cell.
rubric.description: States that the nucleus controls cell activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the control function.

rubric.why: The nucleus stores and passes on hereditary information; the nucleolus helps form ribosomes.
rubric.description: States a further function of the nucleus or nucleolus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying hereditary information storage or transfer, or the nucleolus's role in ribosome formation.

modelAnswer: The nucleus is surrounded by a double-membraned nuclear envelope containing pores.
The inside of the nucleus contains nucleoplasm.
Chromatin, made of DNA and proteins, is present in the nucleus and forms chromosomes during cell division.
The nucleus controls and coordinates the activities of the cell.
It stores hereditary information and passes it on to daughter cells; the nucleolus helps form ribosomes.
